messages.subject: Some problems with predictions of Bayesian multinomial model
parts:
Good afternoon! 
I would like to get the predictions of the model but Stan tells me that something is wrong. Please, help me to understand the problem

predictions_of_bayesian_multi_logit <- "
data {
    int N;                                         // number of individuals 
    int<lower=2> K;                        // number of alternatives
    int<lower=1> D;                        // number of individual predictors
    int<lower=1> C;                        // number of cards for train sample
    int<lower=1> C_tilde;               // number of cards for test sample
    matrix[K, D] X[N, C];                 // individual predictors for train sample
    matrix[K,D] X_tilde[N, C_tilde]; // individual predictors for test sample
    int<lower=1,upper=5> y[N, C];  // outcomes 
}
parameters {
    vector[D] beta;
}
model {
    for (d in 1:D)
        beta[d] ~ normal(0, 5);
    for (n in 1:N)
        for (c in 1:C)
        y[n, c] ~ categorical_logit(X[n, c]*beta);
}
generated quantities {
    int<lower=1,upper=5> y_tilde[N, C_tilde];
    for (n in 1:N)
    for (c in 1:C_tilde)
        y_tilde[n, c] = categorical_logit(X_tilde[n, c]*beta);
}
" 

data_for_aggregate_logit <- list(N = N, y = y_train, X = X_train, X_tilde = X_test, D = D, C = C, C_tilde = C_tilde, K = K)
fit_aggregate_logit <- stan(model_code = predictions_of_bayesian_multi_logit, data = data_for_aggregate_logit, iter = 1000, chains = 4) 

When I`m trying to fit the model, Stan tells me the following:


SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

No matches for: 

  categorical_logit(vector)

Function categorical_logit not found.

ERROR at line 26

 24:        for (n in 1:N)
 25:        for (c in 1:C_tilde)
 26:            y_tilde[n, c] = categorical_logit(X_tilde[n, c]*beta);
                                                                     ^
 27:    }


Do you know how the given problem can be solved? Thanks in advance!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Some problems with predictions of Bayesian multinomial model

Use categorical_logit_rng() in generated quantities. rng stands for random number generator.
